claim.text: A project crawl is constrained to one origin, obeys applicable robots rules across queue entries and redirects, records URL-scoped observations/findings, respects page/time/request budgets, and surfaces persisted coverage limits; the captured PostgreSQL tests use the same disposable local database whose migration state the gate checks.

payload.challenge: No material finding survives. The bound source verifies; the gate preflight explicitly checks serpvera_dev on the disposable socket, and its test stage runs env -u DATABASE_URL while passing the identical PG_SOCKET_DIR, PGPORT, PGUSER, and PGDATABASE. The API store falls back to that socket/database when DATABASE_URL is absent, and node-postgres resolves the explicitly passed PGPORT/PGUSER. Raw logs show migration 0027 preflight passed, DB tests force-executed with 81/81 passing, API tests force-executed with 136/136 passing including real PostgreSQL crawl persistence, and the final test tasks were 14/14 successful with 0 cached. The capture supports the bounded crawl and same-database claim.
